q: If, upon completion of the Contract Document Phase, the Owner has paid the Architect a total of only P1,700,000.00 against the P2,000,000.00 PF, is the Owner in compliance with the Schedule of Payments?
o: Yes — 90% is only reached after the Bidding Phase, so P1,700,000.00 is sufficient at the Contract Document stage
No — the cumulative total due at that stage is 90% of the PF, or P1,800,000.00, so the Owner is short by P100,000.00
No — the cumulative total due at that stage is 100% of the PF
Yes — the Contract Document Phase only requires 80% cumulative payment
n: Completion of the Contract Document Phase should bring cumulative payments to 90% of PF (P1,800,000.00 for a P2,000,000 PF). A running total of P1,700,000.00 falls P100,000.00 short of what is due. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4 (Manner of Payment))
scenario: In a separate engagement, an Owner and an Architect agree on a total Professional Fee (PF) of Two Million Pesos (P2,000,000.00), payable per the Schedule of Payments under SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4.

q: A project site is located in a remote, mountainous area far from the Architect's office, raising questions of accessibility and unusual ground conditions. Which Fee Adjustment Factor does this correspond to?
n: Factor (j), Project Location and Site Conditions, covers unusual site or locational circumstances (such as remoteness or difficult site conditions) that add to the Architect's burden of services. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.5(j))

q: Upon completion and submission of the documents under the Contract Document Phase, how much additional payment is due, and what cumulative percentage does this bring the total to?
o: An additional 60% of the PF, bringing the cumulative total to 100% of the PF
An additional 50% of the PF, bringing the cumulative total to 90% of the PF
An additional 50% of the PF, bringing the cumulative total to 100% of the PF
An additional 40% of the PF, bringing the cumulative total to 80% of the PF
n: Upon completion of the Contract Document Phase, the Owner pays 50% of the PF, or enough to bring the cumulative total to 90% of the PF — the largest single increment in the schedule. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4 (Manner of Payment))

q: An Architect has fully prepared and submitted all documents through the Contract Document Phase (equivalent to 90% of the work), but the Owner then decides not to implement the plans for construction at all. What is the Architect entitled to receive?
o: 50% of the Architect's fee, being only the amount tied to the Contract Document Phase itself
Only the 5% engagement fee paid upon signing of the Service Agreement
Nothing, since no construction ever took place
Compensation equivalent to 90% of the Architect's fee, regardless of whether construction proceeds
n: Once the Architect has completed all documents through the Detailed Design and Contract Documents Phase (90% of the work), the Architect is entitled to 90% of the fee as compensation if the Owner fails to implement the plans and documents for construction — regardless of whether construction ever proceeds. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4.9)

q: Which Fee Adjustment Factor concerns the level, seniority, or cost of the staff the Architect must assign to a project, and the corresponding compensation for that personnel?
n: Factor (m), Architect's Personnel/Architect's Compensation, covers how the staffing level and personnel costs the Architect must commit to a project can affect the appropriate professional fee. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.5(m))

q: Upon completion of the work (i.e., when the Certificate of Completion is issued to the Contractor), the remaining 10% of the Professional Fee is broken down into which two components?
o: 5% for site inspection and 5% for as-built drawings
10% entirely for Periodic Construction Supervision (PCS), with no civil liability component
5% for the Architect's Liability under the Civil Code, and 5% for Periodic Construction Supervision (PCS)
5% for punch-list correction and 5% for final acceptance testing
n: The remaining 10% of the PF, due upon completion of the work, is broken down as 5% for the Architect's liability under the Civil Code and 5% for Periodic Construction Supervision (PCS). (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4 (Manner of Payment))

q: In a project with PF = P5,000,000.00, the Periodic Construction Supervision (PCS) component of the fee not yet earned is P150,000.00 when construction is suspended for eight (8) months (exceeding the 6-month threshold). What should the fee for that remaining PCS work become?
n: Because the suspension exceeds six (6) months, Sec. 6.4.10 requires that the fee for the remaining Periodic Construction Supervision work be doubled — P150,000.00 becomes P300,000.00. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4.10)
scenario: A Service Agreement between an Owner and an Architect fixes the Architect's total Professional Fee (PF) at Five Million Pesos (P5,000,000.00), payable per the Schedule of Payments under SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4.

q: Which of the following pairs correctly matches a Fee Adjustment Factor with its example, as distinguished from a similar-sounding but different factor in SPP Document 202?
o: "Phased Building Occupancies" refers to the stop-and-start-up of the Architect's workforce
"Repeat Work or Repetitive Designs" and "Phased Building Occupancies" refer to exactly the same scenario under SPP Document 202
"Demobilization and Remobilization" refers to reusing the same design across multiple projects

"Repeat Work or Repetitive Designs" refers to reusing the same design across multiple projects, which is different from "Phased Building Occupancies," which refers to staggered turnover/occupancy within a single project
n: Factor (l), Repeat Work or Repetitive Designs, concerns reusing a design across separate projects/sites. Factor (o), Phased Building Occupancies, instead concerns a single project or development being occupied/turned over in stages. Factor (n), Demobilization and Remobilization, is the one that concerns stopping and restarting the workforce. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.5(l), (n), (o))

q: Arrange the following Work Phases in the correct order in which the Architect's Professional Fee is released under the Schedule of Payments: (1) Design Development Phase, (2) Bidding or Negotiation Phase, (3) Signing of the Service Agreement, (4) Contract Document Phase, (5) Schematic Design Phase.
n: The Schedule of Payments runs: signing of the Service Agreement (5%), Schematic Design Phase completion (20% cumulative), Design Development Phase completion (40% cumulative), Contract Document Phase completion (90% cumulative), then the Bidding/Negotiation Phase adjustment (still 90%, but based on the winning bid), before Completion of Work brings the total to 100%. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4 (Manner of Payment))

q: An Architect is engaged to conduct feasibility studies and site-selection analysis before any actual design work begins. Under which Fee Adjustment Factor would this service most likely fall?
o: Scope of Services (pre-design or upstream services)
n: Feasibility studies and site-selection work performed before design begins are pre-design or upstream services, a sub-category of factor (a), Scope of Services. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.5(a))

q: An Architect notices that a fast-tracked project schedule reduces the time available for design decisions, while a protracted (slow) schedule increases decision time. According to SPP Document 202, how might fees be affected by construction schedule changes in either direction?
o: Only an extended schedule can trigger a fee adjustment; a shortened schedule never does
Fees are legally fixed and can never be adjusted for schedule changes
Fees can only ever increase, regardless of whether the schedule is extended or shortened
Fees may be adjusted either upward (for extended Architect involvement) or downward (for reduced decision time), depending on the direction of the schedule change
n: SPP Document 202 notes that when a construction schedule is extended, the Architect's services and compensation must also extend; conversely, if the schedule is fast and protracted, decision times are reduced and fees may be adjusted accordingly (in either direction). (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.5(c))

q: How much additional payment is due to the Architect upon completion of the Design Development Phase, and what is the cumulative amount paid to date?
o: P1,250,000.00 additional, for a cumulative total of P2,250,000.00
P1,000,000.00 additional, for a cumulative total of P2,000,000.00
P1,000,000.00 additional, for a cumulative total of P1,750,000.00
P750,000.00 additional, for a cumulative total of P1,750,000.00
n: 20% of P5,000,000 = P1,000,000.00 additional, bringing the cumulative total to 40% of PF = P2,000,000.00. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4 (Manner of Payment))
scenario: A Service Agreement between an Owner and an Architect fixes the Architect's total Professional Fee (PF) at Five Million Pesos (P5,000,000.00), payable per the Schedule of Payments under SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4.

q: A single set of architectural design and construction documents is completed, one bid package is prepared, and the resulting construction contract with a single general contractor is administered by the Architect. This is the traditional delivery/procurement method known as:
n: This describes the traditional Design-Bid-Build method: complete design and construction documents, one bid package, bidding, and a single construction contract administered by the Architect — as opposed to Sequential Tendering's multiple, staggered bid packages. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.5(b))

q: Why does SPP Document 202 state that its list of Fee Adjustment Factors (Sec. 6.5) is "not exhaustive"?
o: Because only government projects may use factors beyond the fifteen listed
Because the list was left incomplete due to a printing error in the Official Gazette
Because each factor listed already contains its own sub-list of every possible variation
Because the design and construction industry is complex, and unique project factors beyond the listed items may also affect an appropriate fee
n: SPP Document 202 explains that each project is subject to unique factors, so the fifteen listed fee adjustment factors (a to o) are only examples — Owners, Clients, or Architects may identify other factors affecting the cost of professional services. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.5 (Fee Adjustment Factors))

q: Upon completion of the work, how is the remaining P500,000.00 (10% of the PF) broken down between the Architect's civil-liability component and the Periodic Construction Supervision (PCS) component?
o: P150,000.00 for civil liability and P350,000.00 for PCS
P250,000.00 for civil liability and P250,000.00 for PCS
P400,000.00 for civil liability and P100,000.00 for PCS
P500,000.00 for PCS only, with no civil-liability component
n: The remaining 10% of PF (P500,000.00) splits evenly: 5% (P250,000.00) for the Architect's liability under the Civil Code, and 5% (P250,000.00) for Periodic Construction Supervision. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4 (Manner of Payment))
scenario: A Service Agreement between an Owner and an Architect fixes the Architect's total Professional Fee (PF) at Five Million Pesos (P5,000,000.00), payable per the Schedule of Payments under SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4.

q: A complex hospital project requires the Architect to retain and coordinate the work of acoustical, kitchen-equipment, and medical-gas engineers who are not part of the Architect's usual design team. Which Fee Adjustment Factor is most directly implicated?
n: Factor (e), Specialist Consultants, covers the need to retain and coordinate specialized consultants beyond the Architect's typical design team, which increases the scope and cost of professional services. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.5(e))

q: The 5% payment due upon signing of the Service Agreement is computed based on which cost figure?
o: The winning bid or contract price
The SPPCC submitted at the Contract Document Phase
The Statement of Probable Project Construction Cost (SPPCC) included in the Annex of the Service Agreement
n: Sec. 6.4.1 specifies that the Professional Fee for this first payment is computed based on the original Statement of Probable Project Construction Cost (SPPCC) as included in the Annex of the Service Agreement. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4.1)

q: How much additional payment is due to the Architect upon completion of the Contract Document Phase, and what is the cumulative total?
o: P800,000.00 additional, for a cumulative total of P1,600,000.00
P1,000,000.00 additional, for a cumulative total of P2,000,000.00
P900,000.00 additional, for a cumulative total of P1,700,000.00
P1,000,000.00 additional, for a cumulative total of P1,800,000.00
n: 50% of P2,000,000 = P1,000,000.00 additional, bringing the cumulative total to 90% = P1,800,000.00. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4 (Manner of Payment))
scenario: In a separate engagement, an Owner and an Architect agree on a total Professional Fee (PF) of Two Million Pesos (P2,000,000.00), payable per the Schedule of Payments under SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4.

q: A Client is anxious to incorporate the latest, largely untested energy-performance systems and building products into their project, requiring the Architect to do additional research and possibly retain additional specialist consultants. Which Fee Adjustment Factor does this illustrate?
n: Factor (h), New Technologies, covers the unknown risks, additional certifications/testing, and extra research or consultants that may be needed when a Client wants to incorporate the latest building innovations. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.5(h))

q: The payment due upon completion of the Schematic Design Phase is computed based on which cost figure?
o: The SPPCC that is part of the documents submitted at that particular (Schematic Design) stage
The original SPPCC included in the Annex of the Service Agreement
n: Unlike the signing-stage payment (based on the original SPPCC), the Schematic Design, Design Development, and Contract Document phase payments are each computed based on the updated SPPCC submitted together with the documents at that particular stage. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4 (Manner of Payment))

q: Under the Schedule of Payments, may the Owner make partial payments to the Architect during any given stage of the work?
o: No, partial payments are prohibited under any circumstance
No, payments may only be made in full lump sums at the end of each phase
Yes, provided such partial payments remain within the framework of the manner of payments outlined in Sec. 6.4
Yes, but only if the Architect waives the remainder of that stage's payment
n: The Owner can make partial payments during each of the various stages of the Architect's work, upon the Architect's request, provided such payments stay within the framework of the manner of payments outlined in the Schedule of Payments. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4.7)

q: An Architect is engaged to renovate a decades-old commercial building, requiring extensive as-built verification and dealing with unforeseen existing conditions not present in new construction. Which Fee Adjustment Factor applies?
o: Renovation to Existing Buildings (versus New Construction)
n: Factor (k), Renovation to Existing Buildings (versus New Construction), recognizes that renovation work carries added complexity — such as verifying existing/as-built conditions — not present in new construction. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.5(k))

q: Within how many days after the award to the winning bidder or bidders must the Owner adjust the payment to the Architect during the Bidding or Negotiation Phase?
n: Within 15 days after the contract award to the winning bidder(s), the payment to the Architect must be adjusted so that total payments equal 90% of the Professional Fee. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4 (Manner of Payment))

q: A building project is erected in phases, with different portions constructed at different periods of time, extending the overall construction period. What happens to the fee for services rendered during the Construction Phase in this situation?
o: The charges pertaining to services rendered during the Construction Phase are adjusted proportionately to reflect the extended burden of services
The fee remains fixed exactly as originally computed, with no adjustment
The entire Professional Fee is recomputed from zero based on a new Service Agreement
The Architect forfeits any right to additional compensation for the extended period
n: When portions of the building(s) are erected at different periods, thereby increasing the construction period and the Architect's burden of services, the charges for services rendered during the Construction Phase are adjusted proportionately. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4.10)

q: A project is halted for several months due to a Client's funding delay, then later resumed, requiring the Architect to stand down and later reassemble the project team ("stop and start-up of workforce"). Which Fee Adjustment Factor covers this?
n: Factor (n), Demobilization and Remobilization, specifically addresses the stop-and-start-up of the Architect's workforce that occurs when a project is paused and later resumed. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.5(n))

q: The final balance of the Architect's fee, paid upon completion of the work, is computed based on which cost figure?
o: The original SPPCC in the Service Agreement
The SPPCC submitted at the Design Development Phase
n: Upon completion of the work, the Architect's remaining balance is computed based on the Final Project Construction Cost (FPCC) — the actual, as-built construction cost, rather than any of the earlier probable-cost estimates. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4 (Manner of Payment))

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes "suspension of work" from "non-implementation" under the Schedule of Payments' Things to Note?
o: There is no meaningful difference — both terms describe the same scenario under SPP Document 202
Both situations entitle the Architect to exactly 90% of the fee in every case

Suspension entitles the Architect only to the amount due at the stage reached when work stopped, while non-implementation (after all Contract Documents are completed) entitles the Architect to 90% of the fee regardless of whether construction proceeds
Suspension entitles the Architect to 100% of the fee, while non-implementation entitles the Architect to nothing
n: Suspension/abandonment (Sec. 6.4.8) ties compensation to whatever stage the work had reached when it stopped. Non-implementation (Sec. 6.4.9) specifically addresses the case where all Contract Documents were already completed (90% of the work) but the Owner simply chooses not to build — in that case the Architect is still owed 90% of the fee. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4.8-6.4.9)

q: How many Fee Adjustment Factors, at minimum, does SPP Document 202 expressly list (labeled a through o)?
n: SPP Document 202 lists fifteen (15) fee adjustment factors, lettered (a) through (o), while noting that the list is not exhaustive. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.5)

q: How much is the Architect entitled to receive upon signing of the Service Agreement?
n: 5% of the P5,000,000 PF = P250,000.00, payable upon signing of the Service Agreement, computed based on the original SPPCC in the Annex of the Service Agreement. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4.1)
scenario: A Service Agreement between an Owner and an Architect fixes the Architect's total Professional Fee (PF) at Five Million Pesos (P5,000,000.00), payable per the Schedule of Payments under SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4.

q: Which Fee Adjustment Factor covers Sequential Tendering, Design-Bid-Build, Design-Build, and Public-Private Partnerships (PPP)?
o: Project Delivery Method and Construction Procurement
n: Factor (b), Project Delivery Method and Construction Procurement, expressly lists Sequential Tendering, Design-Bid-Build, Design-Build, and Public-Private Partnerships (PPP) as its sub-categories. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.5(b))

q: Under SPP Document 202, the Schedule of Payments (Sec. 6.4) and the Fee Adjustment Factors (Sec. 6.5) both fall under which broader chapter of the document?
n: Sections 6.4 and 6.5 are provisions within Sec. 6 (Regular Design Services) of SPP Document 202, covering how the Architect's Professional Fee for regular design services is released over time and what may cause that fee to be adjusted. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4 (Manner of Payment))

q: How much additional payment is due to the Architect upon completion of the Contract Document Phase, and what is the cumulative amount paid to date?
o: P2,500,000.00 additional, for a cumulative total of P5,000,000.00
P2,000,000.00 additional, for a cumulative total of P4,000,000.00
P2,250,000.00 additional, for a cumulative total of P4,250,000.00
P2,500,000.00 additional, for a cumulative total of P4,500,000.00
n: 50% of P5,000,000 = P2,500,000.00 additional, bringing the cumulative total to 90% of PF = P4,500,000.00. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4 (Manner of Payment))
scenario: A Service Agreement between an Owner and an Architect fixes the Architect's total Professional Fee (PF) at Five Million Pesos (P5,000,000.00), payable per the Schedule of Payments under SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4.

q: Which Fee Adjustment Factor is illustrated by a project that must be fast-tracked because the building must be ready for a specific tenant move-in date, requiring the Architect to hire additional staff and pay overtime?
n: Factor (c), Project or Construction Schedules, covers fast-tracked or otherwise pressured project timelines that require additional Architect staffing, overtime pay, and re-scheduling of other work — all justifying an adjustment to the fee. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.5(c))

q: According to SPP Document 202, a fee adjustment factor can sometimes work in the Architect's favor by increasing the fee, but the document also gives an example of a factor that could do the opposite. Which of the following is that example?
o: Limited project documentation, or elimination of an entire phase such as bidding and contract negotiation if undertaken by the Owner
A requirement for the Architect to use Building Information Modeling (BIM)
A construction schedule extended beyond the original completion date
A project located more than 100 kilometers from the Architect's office
n: The document notes that a fee adjustment factor may sometimes reduce the fee — for example, limited project documentation, or the elimination of an entire phase (such as bidding and contract negotiation) if the Owner undertakes that phase directly. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.5 (Fee Adjustment Factors))

q: How much is due to the Architect upon signing of the Service Agreement, and how much additional is due upon completion of the Schematic Design Phase?
o: P200,000.00 upon signing; an additional P300,000.00 upon Schematic Design completion
P100,000.00 upon signing; an additional P300,000.00 upon Schematic Design completion
P100,000.00 upon signing; an additional P200,000.00 upon Schematic Design completion
P100,000.00 upon signing; an additional P400,000.00 upon Schematic Design completion
n: 5% of P2,000,000 = P100,000.00 upon signing; 15% of P2,000,000 = P300,000.00 more upon Schematic Design Phase completion, bringing the cumulative total to 20% (P400,000.00). (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4 (Manner of Payment))
scenario: In a separate engagement, an Owner and an Architect agree on a total Professional Fee (PF) of Two Million Pesos (P2,000,000.00), payable per the Schedule of Payments under SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4.

q: A project sits within a jurisdiction that requires multiple separate agency approvals — a local zoning board, a heritage-conservation council, and a fire-safety board — each adding a review cycle. Which Fee Adjustment Factor covers this circumstance?
n: Factor (f), Approvals and Authorities Having Jurisdiction, addresses the added time and effort of securing approvals from multiple regulatory bodies, which can justify a fee adjustment. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.5(f))

q: Upon completion and submission of the documents under the Schematic Design Phase, how much additional payment is the Owner obliged to pay the Architect, and what is the cumulative total at that point?
o: An additional 15% of the PF, bringing the cumulative total to 35% of the PF
An additional 10% of the PF, bringing the cumulative total to 15% of the PF
An additional 20% of the PF, bringing the cumulative total to 25% of the PF
An additional 15% of the PF, bringing the cumulative total to 20% of the PF
n: Upon completion of the Schematic Design Phase, the Owner pays a sum equal to 15% of the PF (or enough to bring cumulative payments to 20% of the PF, deducting what was already paid upon signing). (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4 (Manner of Payment))

q: Upon completion of the work, how much does the Architect receive for the civil-liability component versus the Periodic Construction Supervision (PCS) component?
o: P200,000.00 for civil liability and no separate amount for PCS
P100,000.00 for civil liability and P100,000.00 for PCS
P50,000.00 for civil liability and P150,000.00 for PCS
P100,000.00 for civil liability and P50,000.00 for PCS
n: The remaining 10% of the P2,000,000 PF (P200,000.00) splits evenly into 5% (P100,000.00) for civil liability and 5% (P100,000.00) for Periodic Construction Supervision. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4 (Manner of Payment))
scenario: In a separate engagement, an Owner and an Architect agree on a total Professional Fee (PF) of Two Million Pesos (P2,000,000.00), payable per the Schedule of Payments under SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4.

q: A construction contract is structured as a "Cost Plus" or Unit Price contract (rather than a Stipulated Sum contract), requiring the Architect to prepare more frequent and detailed Certificates for Payment. Which Fee Adjustment Factor is most directly implicated?
o: Project Delivery Method and Construction Procurement
n: Factor (i), Construction Administration, covers services beyond the reasonable standard of care during field review and contract administration — including the added Certificate-for-Payment work required by Cost Plus or Unit Price contracts, as opposed to Stipulated Sum contracts. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.5(i))

q: Upon completion and submission of the documents under the Design Development Phase, how much additional payment is due, and what cumulative percentage of the PF does this bring the total to?
o: An additional 25% of the PF, bringing the cumulative total to 45% of the PF
An additional 15% of the PF, bringing the cumulative total to 35% of the PF
An additional 20% of the PF, bringing the cumulative total to 40% of the PF
An additional 20% of the PF, bringing the cumulative total to 50% of the PF
n: Upon completion of the Design Development Phase, the Owner pays 20% of the PF, or enough to bring the cumulative total to 40% of the PF (net of what was already paid). (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4 (Manner of Payment))

q: If the Architect's work is abandoned or suspended in whole or in part, how much must the Owner pay the Architect?
o: Nothing, since the Architect did not complete the engagement
The full 100% of the Professional Fee regardless of the stage reached
The amount due corresponding to the stage of suspension or abandonment of the work
Only the 5% engagement fee paid upon signing, with all other payments forfeited
n: When the Architect's work is abandoned or suspended, whether wholly or partly, the Owner must pay the Architect for services rendered corresponding to the amount due at the stage the work had reached when suspension or abandonment occurred. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4.8)

q: A fast-food chain hires an Architect to design ten (10) identical branch outlets to be built in different locations, all using essentially the same design. Which Fee Adjustment Factor is most relevant to how this repeated work may affect the fee?
n: Factor (l), Repeat Work or Repetitive Designs, addresses situations where a design (or substantially the same design) is reused across multiple projects or sites, which can affect the appropriate fee level (often reducing per-unit cost due to design reuse). (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.5(l))

q: During the Bidding or Negotiation Phase, the payment to the Architect is adjusted so that it amounts to a sum equivalent to 90% of the Professional Fee, computed based on which figure?
o: The SPPCC submitted at the Contract Document Phase
The original SPPCC in the Service Agreement
The lowest bona fide bid, or the winning bid price
n: At the Bidding/Negotiation Phase, the 90%-of-PF figure is recomputed based on the lowest bona fide bid or bids, or upon the winning bid price — replacing the SPPCC-based estimate used earlier. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4 (Manner of Payment))

q: If the suspension of construction under a phased-construction scenario exceeds a period of six (6) months, what happens to the fee for the remaining Periodic Construction Supervision (PCS) work?
o: The fee for the remaining PCS work shall be reduced by half
The fee for the remaining PCS work is forfeited entirely
The fee for the remaining PCS work shall be doubled
The fee for the remaining PCS work stays exactly the same, unadjusted
n: SPP Document 202 provides that when the suspension of construction exceeds six (6) months, the fee for the remaining works (Periodic Construction Supervision) shall be doubled, in recognition of the extended, discontinuous demand on the Architect's services. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4.10)

q: A large mixed-use development is designed so that its residential tower is occupied and operating months before the retail podium below it is turned over, requiring the Architect to coordinate separate turnover and supervision efforts for each portion. Which Fee Adjustment Factor covers this circumstance?
n: Factor (o), Phased Building Occupancies, covers projects where different portions of a building or development are occupied at different times, each requiring separate coordination and supervision efforts from the Architect. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.5(o))

q: Progress billing on the remaining 10% of the Architect's fee (covering the Construction Phase) may be done based on which cost figure?
o: The Final Project Construction Cost (FPCC) only
The original Statement of Probable Project Construction Cost (SPPCC)
An arbitrary percentage set solely by the Contractor
n: Progress billing on the remaining 10% of the Architect's fee during the Construction Phase can be done based on the original Statement of Probable Project Construction Cost (SPPCC), with the final balance later trued up against the FPCC upon completion of the work. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4 (Manner of Payment))

q: SPP Document 202 lists "Scope of Services" as a fee adjustment factor. Which of the following is NOT one of the sub-categories mentioned under this factor?
n: Under factor (a), Scope of Services, SPP Document 202 lists pre-design/upstream services, traditional architectural design services, and other services. Public-Private Partnerships (PPP) is instead listed under factor (b), Project Delivery Method and Construction Procurement. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.5(a))

q: A Client requests LEED, GREEN, or BERDE certification for a project, requiring the Architect to manage third-party certification and documentation. Under SPP Document 202's discussion of fee adjustment considerations, this is most closely associated with which factor?
n: SPP Document 202 discusses third-party green-building certification (LEED, GREEN, BERDE) in connection with new construction technologies and innovations, since such certifications often accompany the adoption of new building products, systems, or performance standards. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.5(h))

q: How much additional payment is due to the Architect upon completion of the Schematic Design Phase, and what is the cumulative amount paid to date?
o: P500,000.00 additional, for a cumulative total of P750,000.00
P1,000,000.00 additional, for a cumulative total of P1,250,000.00
P750,000.00 additional, for a cumulative total of P1,000,000.00
P750,000.00 additional, for a cumulative total of P750,000.00
n: 15% of P5,000,000 = P750,000.00 additional, bringing the cumulative total to 20% of PF = P1,000,000.00 (the P250,000 already paid upon signing is credited against this amount). (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4 (Manner of Payment))
scenario: A Service Agreement between an Owner and an Architect fixes the Architect's total Professional Fee (PF) at Five Million Pesos (P5,000,000.00), payable per the Schedule of Payments under SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4.

q: An Owner decides to separate the construction documents into multiple bid packages — one for site work, another for foundations, and another for the superstructure — released for bidding at different times in sequence. This construction-procurement approach is best described as:
n: Sequential Tendering involves separating the contract documents (bid documents, specifications, and construction drawings) into separate packages to receive multiple bids for different parts of the work, usually released in the sequence of construction (e.g., site work, then foundations). Preparing multiple bid packages and administering several contracts requires additional services from the Architect, adjusting the fee accordingly. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.5(b))

q: What is the basic premise of the Schedule of Payments in Sec. 6.4 of SPP Document 202?
o: Payments to the Architect are released in stages tied to the phases of the Architect's work, as percentages of the agreed Professional Fee (PF)
The Architect is paid only after the project obtains its Certificate of Occupancy
The entire Professional Fee is paid in a single lump sum after construction is complete
Payments are fixed peso amounts unrelated to the Professional Fee or project phase
n: Sec. 6.4 states that payments to the Architect on account of the agreed Professional Fee shall be made by the Owner at the different phases of the Architect's work, each phase corresponding to a specified percentage of the PF. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4 (Manner of Payment))

q: Assuming the winning bid price validates the same PF base, what cumulative amount should the Architect have received by the end of the Bidding or Negotiation Phase?
n: By the end of the Bidding/Negotiation Phase, cumulative payments must equal 90% of the PF — P4,500,000.00 — though this figure is now recomputed against the winning bid price rather than the SPPCC used at the Contract Document stage. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4 (Manner of Payment))
scenario: A Service Agreement between an Owner and an Architect fixes the Architect's total Professional Fee (PF) at Five Million Pesos (P5,000,000.00), payable per the Schedule of Payments under SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4.

q: A Client requires the Architect to develop all project documentation using a Building Information Model (BIM) and to provide electronic documents in several formats for different parties involved in the project. Which Fee Adjustment Factor does this illustrate?
n: Factor (d), Project Documentation and Computer Modeling, specifically addresses unique documentation formats, BIM requirements, and providing electronic documents in multiple formats to different parties — all of which can be time-consuming and warrant a fee adjustment. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.5(d))

q: Upon signing of the Service Agreement, what percentage of the Professional Fee (PF) is due to the Architect as engagement/acceptance fee covering the mobilization component of the services?
n: Sec. 6.4.1 provides that upon signing of the Service Agreement, an amount equivalent to 5% of the agreed Professional Fee is paid as engagement or acceptance fee, covering the mobilization component of the Architect's services. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4.1)

q: What is the cumulative amount the Architect should have received by the time the Design Development Phase is completed?
n: By completion of the Design Development Phase, cumulative payments must equal 40% of the P2,000,000 PF = P800,000.00. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4 (Manner of Payment))
scenario: In a separate engagement, an Owner and an Architect agree on a total Professional Fee (PF) of Two Million Pesos (P2,000,000.00), payable per the Schedule of Payments under SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4.

q: Which Fee Adjustment Factor is distinct from, but closely related to, "Approvals and Authorities Having Jurisdiction," and refers instead to the preparation and processing of shop drawings, samples, and similar documents required during construction?
n: Factor (g), Submittals, is listed separately from factor (f), Approvals and Authorities Having Jurisdiction — the former concerns the volume/complexity of submittals (such as shop drawings) the Architect must review, while the latter concerns regulatory approval processes. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.5(g))

q: The payment due upon completion of the Schematic Design Phase must be made by the Owner within how many days after submission of the documents?
n: The Schedule of Payments requires the Owner to pay the corresponding amount not more than 15 days after the Architect submits the required documents for that phase — the same 15-day window applies at the Schematic Design, Design Development, and Contract Document phases. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4 (Manner of Payment))
